claim.pdf_says: DIVIDE { identifier-1 / literal-1 } INTO { identifier-2 / literal-2 } -- both operand groups are printed with true BRACES (curly '{' ... '}'), stacked over two lines. Same in Format 5: DIVIDE { identifier-2 / literal-2 } BY { identifier-1 / literal-1 }.
claim.markdown_says:
```
           ⌐ identifier-1 ¬        ⌐ identifier-2 ¬
DIVIDE     |              | INTO   |               |
           └ literal-1   ┘        └ literal-2    ┘
```  (identical corner-glyph delimiter used again in Format 5)
claim.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.6.2/5.2.6.3 a BRACE means exactly one of the stacked alternatives SHALL be chosen, while a BRACKET means at most one (the whole group may be omitted). The markdown renders the PDF's braces with the corner glyphs ⌐ ¬ └ ┘, which in this very document's own convention are the BRACKET shape -- Formats 1, 2 and 3 of the same DIVIDE statement (page 644) render braces as ⎧⎨⎩ / ⎫⎬⎭ and brackets as ⎡⎣ / ⎤⎦. Read as brackets, Formats 4 and 5 would falsely permit 'DIVIDE INTO ...' with the dividend/divisor operand omitted. Formats 4 and 5 are the only DIVIDE formats in the file left in the un-normalized OCR glyph set.

verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed on all four legs; I tried to refute it and could not.

(1) WHAT THE PDF PRINTS. Rendered specs page 645 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v645/spec_p645.png) and cropped the operand rows of both formats at 3x (crop_f4.png, crop_f5.png). Format 4 prints DIVIDE followed by a delimiter with the unmistakable middle cusp and tapered tips of a CURLY BRACE around the identifier-1 / literal-1 stack, then INTO followed by a second curly brace around identifier-2 / literal-2. Format 5 is identical in shape around identifier-2 / literal-2 and identifier-1 / literal-1. These are braces, not brackets -- the shape is unambiguous at that magnification, and it contrasts directly with the ON SIZE ERROR delimiter lower on the same page, which I cropped separately (crop_f4_sizeerr.png) and which prints as a square-cornered BRACKET with a straight choice-indicator bar just inside it. So page 645 itself contains both glyph shapes side by side, and they are visibly different.

(2) WHAT THE MARKDOWN PRINTS. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 26698-26708 (Format 4) and 26712-26722 (Format 5) match the claimed quotation character for character, including the trailing-space alignment. Confirmed the operand delimiter is U+2310 / U+00AC on the top row, ASCII '|' on the middle row, U+2514 / U+2518 on the bottom row.

(3) IS THE CORNER GLYPH REALLY THE BRACKET SHAPE IN THIS FILE'S CONVENTION? Yes. A whole-file glyph census gives the normalized sets as brace = U+23A7/23A8/23A9 (455/279/452) and U+23AB/23AC/23AD, bracket = U+23A1/23A3 (199/196) and U+23A4/23A6. The corner glyphs are rare un-normalized residue: U+2310 x18, U+00AC x15, U+2514 x25, U+2518 x29, U+230A x6, U+2308 x2, confined to pages 203, 389, 632, 635, 645 and 799 (the U+2514/U+2518 bulk elsewhere is flowchart box art on pages 1142-1186). Two things follow. First, the corner glyphs draw a square-cornered rectangle, which is geometrically the same shape as the file's normalized BRACKET glyphs and geometrically distinct from the cusped brace glyphs. Second, where the residue appears elsewhere it does in fact stand for brackets: page 635 line 26326 uses '⌐ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 ¬' for the optional INVALID KEY group of DELETE, and page 389 line 16703 uses '⌐ source-clause ¬ / └ value-clause ┘' for the optional source/sum/value stack. So a reader applying this file's own convention reads page 645's operand delimiter as a bracket.

(4) DOES IT CHANGE NORMATIVE MEANING? Yes. Verified the cited rules verbatim in the same file: 5.2.6.2 (line 2693) says a bracketed portion 'may be explicitly specified or that portion of the general format may be omitted'; 5.2.6.3 (line 2698) says a braced portion 'shall be explicitly specified or is implicitly selected'. Turning the dividend/divisor brace into a bracket demotes a mandatory operand to an omittable one, admitting the nonsense form 'DIVIDE INTO x GIVING y REMAINDER z'. Nothing on page 645 compensates: unlike Formats 1-3 on page 644, which each carry an explanatory 'Figure notes' block, Formats 4 and 5 carry no figure notes at all. Syntax rules 1 and 3 constrain the CATEGORY of identifier-1/literal-1 but never state that the operand is required, so they do not repair the loss.

Refutation attempts that failed: the delimiter is not merely reflowed or line-wrapped (the glyph identity itself changed); it is not page-break furniture; the claim misquotes neither source; and 'single corner form = brace, doubled corner form = bracket' is not a rescuing convention -- it is documented nowhere, and the single form demonstrably means bracket on pages 389 and 635.
verdict.corrected_description:
CONFIRMED, with the scope of the defect slightly wider than described. Page 645 is the only page where the two DIVIDE remainder formats survive in the un-normalized OCR glyph set, and that page loses TWO distinct normative choice indicators, not one.

(a) THE CLAIMED DEFECT, confirmed exactly as stated. The PDF prints true curly braces around the dividend/divisor stacks in Format 4 ('DIVIDE {identifier-1 / literal-1} INTO {identifier-2 / literal-2}') and Format 5 ('DIVIDE {identifier-2 / literal-2} BY {identifier-1 / literal-1}'). specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 26699-26701 and 26713-26715 render both with the corner glyphs U+2310/U+00AC over U+2514/U+2518 -- the square-cornered rectangle that is this file's BRACKET shape (cf. its normalized brackets U+23A1/23A3/23A4/23A6, and its normalized braces U+23A7/23A8/23A9 used for the very same operand groups in Formats 1-3 on page 644 at lines 26634-26636, 26653-26655, 26673-26675). Per 5.2.6.3 the brace makes the operand mandatory; read as the bracket of 5.2.6.2 it becomes omittable.

(b) AN AGGRAVATING DETAIL THE CLAIM DOES NOT MENTION. The middle row of the markdown's operand box is rendered with a pair of ASCII '|' characters ('DIVIDE     |              | INTO   |               |'). In this document '|' is itself a normative glyph -- the CHOICE INDICATOR of 5.2.6.4. So the transcribed operand group can be misread not merely as a bracket but as a bracket enclosing choice indicators, i.e. 'zero or more of identifier-1 / literal-1, in any order' -- a strictly worse reading than the plain-bracket one the claim describes.

(c) A SECOND LOST INDICATOR ON THE SAME PAGE. In the PDF, the ON SIZE ERROR group of Formats 4 and 5 is a BRACKET enclosing CHOICE INDICATOR bars ('[ | ON SIZE ERROR ... | NOT ON SIZE ERROR ... | ]'), which per 5.2.6.4 permits zero or more of the alternatives, each at most once, in any order -- so both handlers may appear on one statement. The markdown renders it as '⌐⌐ ... ¬¬' / '⌊⌊ ... ┘┘' (lines 26705-26706 and 26719-26720), collapsing bracket and bar into an undifferentiated doubled corner. Page 644 repaired exactly this for Formats 1-3 with an explicit 'Figure notes' warning citing 5.2.6.4; page 645 has no figure notes whatsoever, so Formats 4 and 5 lose both the brace marking and that compensating annotation.

Remedy: re-render both formats on page 645 using the file's normalized glyphs -- U+23A7/23A8/23A9 and U+23AB/23AC/23AD for the two operand stacks, U+23A1/23A3/23A4/23A6 plus explicit '|' bars for the ON SIZE ERROR group -- and add the same 'Figure notes' block (underlined required words plus the 5.2.6.4 choice-indicator warning) that Formats 1-3 already carry.
